text: Immature, later known as IMx, is an American R&B boy band managed by record producer Chris Stokes, formed in Los Angeles, California in 1991 by Marques "Batman" Houston (born August 4, 1981), Jerome "Romeo" Jones (born October 25, 1981), and Don "Half Pint" Santos. Kelton "LDB" Kessee (born January 2, 1981), the group's drummer at the time, joined full-time in 1994 after Santos was removed due to his parents pulling him from the group following the filming of House Party 3. The group released four albums under the Immature name: On Our Worst Behavior (1992), which included original member Santos and featured singles "Da Munchies", "I Wanna Know U That Way", "Be My Girl", and "Tear It Up (On Our Worst Behavior)", the latter of which appeared on the Bebe's Kids soundtrack and reached number 29 on Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs despite the album not charting on Billboard's charts; Playtyme Is Over (1994), released after signing with MCA Records and featuring singles "Never Lie" (their biggest hit), "Constantly", and "I Don't Mind", which peaked at number 88 on the Billboard 200 and number 26 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums; We Got It (1995), featuring singles "We Got It", "Lover's Groove", and "Please Don't Go", which peaked at number 76 on the Billboard 200 and number 14 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums; and The Journey (1997), their final album under the Immature name, featuring singles "I'm Not a Fool", "Give Up The Ghost" (featuring Bizzy Bone), and "Extra, Extra" (written by and featuring Keith Sweat), which peaked at number 92 on the Billboard 200 and number 20 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums. In 1999, the group changed their name to IMx, feeling "Immature" no longer reflected them, and released Introducing IMx, their fifth album, featuring singles "Stay the Night", "Keep It On the Low", and "In & Out of Love", which peaked at number 101 on the Billboard 200 and number 31 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums. On August 21, 2001, IMx released their sixth album, IMx, after signing with TUG Entertainment and New Line Records (now WaterTower Music), featuring singles "First Time", "Beautiful (You Are)", "Clap Your Hands Pt. 1", and "Ain't No Need" (which appeared on the soundtrack for The Adventures of Pluto Nash), peaking at number 126 on the Billboard 200 and number 26 on Billboard's Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums. The group also released a Greatest Hits album on February 27, 2001, featuring popular singles from the past nine years, including remixes and guest appearances such as Monteco's "Is It Me?". The song "Keep It On the Low" was used as the theme song for House Party 4: Down to the Last Minute, in which the group also starred. Immature branched out into film and television, appearing in House Party 3 and House Party 4: Down to the Last Minute, and on shows such as A Different World, Sister, Sister, Family Matters, Soul Train, and All That, where they collaborated with Kel Mitchell on the hit song "Watch Me Do My Thing" from the All That soundtrack. In 2002, the group disbanded. Houston and Jones (under the name Young Rome) pursued solo careers, with Houston releasing his debut solo album MH in 2003, followed by Food for Thought in 2004, and later releasing Naked (2005), Veteran (2007), Mr. Houston (2009), Mattress Music (2010), and Famous (2013). Jones also released his debut solo album, Food for Thought, in 2004. Houston and Jones both starred in the dance film You Got Served (2004), with Houston also co-starring in Fat Albert (2004) and landing a lead role in the UPN comedy sitcom Cuts, and appearing as Roger on Sister, Sister (1994–1998). In 2007, Houston starred in the horror film Somebody Help Me. The track "Tamika" appeared on the Sister, Sister episode "A Friend in Deed", which aired on October 29, 1997, where the group performed as themselves at a school fundraiser. In early 2015, the band reunited to release a comeback EP titled Remember, changing their name back to Immature, featuring mature-sounding remakes of "Never Lie" and "Please Don't Go" along with new songs "Let Me Find Out", "Oh My", and "Best Sex". On November 6, 2013, Immature performed their first show since reuniting at Club Nokia in Los Angeles with Next and Dru Hill. In September 2019, Immature announced their #TBTour with special guests Ray J, B5, and J. Holiday.
